title: Electoral Analysis
subtitle: A standing observatory of the Spanish vote
question: What does an electorate do between elections, and how much of it shows up on the night?
scope: Elections are covered as events and analysed as events, which is the one frame that guarantees you miss the movement. The interesting part happens in the eighteen months nobody is filming.

This topic is built as an observatory rather than a series of post-mortems: short tracking notes written while something is still moving, one-off insights when a number is worth isolating, and full analyses of past elections once the result can be read against what preceded it.
Scope is by country. For now — and for the foreseeable future — that country is Spain, where the data is good, the calendar is busy, and the party system rewards being read carefully.

method.name: Survey aggregation
method.note: Published polling pooled with house effects and field dates handled explicitly rather than averaged away.

method.name: Time-series forecasting
method.note: Classical series work combined with recurrent nets, as used for decision-makers rather than for headlines.

method.name: Vote transfer
method.note: Estimating where a bloc's vote went, not only that it shrank.

method.name: Territorial breakdown
method.note: Province and municipality level, because national aggregates hide the seat arithmetic.
